collection_description: The latest posted versions of our research on extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma (EMC).

publications.title: NR4A3 Fusion-Junction Antisense Gapmers for Extraskeletal Myxoid Chondrosarcoma: Reagents, Test Articles and a Pre-Registrable Knockdown Experiment
publications.author: Tristan McRae
publications.summary: Develops computational antisense designs for EMC fusion transcripts and a proposed experiment to test whether they can distinguish the fusion from normal parent transcripts. Model junctions must be confirmed before testing; selective knockdown and therapeutic benefit have not been demonstrated.

publications.title: CSPG4 tissue RNA enrichment in extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma depends on comparator and sequencing year
publications.author: Tristan D. McRae
publications.summary: Compares a fixed panel of candidate genes across public tumour RNA datasets. CSPG4 meets the study's prioritization rule, but sensitivity to comparison groups and sequencing year limits the result. The study motivates tissue validation and does not establish accessible protein or treatment efficacy.

publications.title: A fusion-junction vaccine in extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma: what can be established today, and the capabilities that would change it
publications.author: Tristan D. McRae
publications.summary: Examines computational evidence for a vaccine aimed at EMC fusion junctions. Predicted population coverage changes substantially with the prediction method, allele panel and threshold. The paper identifies limits and evidence needed next; predicted binding does not establish immune responses or clinical benefit.

publications.title: Almost every gene set reads higher in the index arm: a size-matched empirical null for small rare-tumour expression series, and what it leaves of the EWSR1::NR4A3 direct-target catalogue
publications.author: Tristan D. McRae
publications.summary: Shows how small tumour expression studies can make many gene sets appear elevated. A comparison with random gene sets of the same size helps assess which signals are distinctive. Applied to EMC, the analysis separates tumour-associated expression from evidence that a gene is driven by the fusion.

publications.title: Reading-frame constraints and retained RG content in NR4A3 fusion models of extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma
publications.author: Tristan McRae
publications.summary: Examines reading-frame constraints and retained RG content in computational models of NR4A3 fusions associated with extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma.
